extracted.intended_audience: Reviewers assigned to Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing peer reviews for submissions to Transactions on Machine Learning Research, including responsibilities, timelines, review content/format, conflict/ethics rules, and certification/recommendation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double blind
rubrics_metrics.description: The TMLR review process is meant to be double blind. The identities of the authors of a submission will be kept from the reviewers, and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are expected not to take any actions that would violate this double blind state, including not actively seeking to find out the identity of the authors (e.g., by searching for related presentations online or preprints on arXiv). Generally, perform searches on related work only after a preliminary read of the submission. If you accidentally discover the identity of the authors and believe it may influence your judgment, contact the Action Editor (AE) so they may determine whether you should be unassigned from the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open reviewing / public visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as all reviews are submitted for a submission, they will become publicly visible (but anonymous). The authors' response to your review and subsequent discussion will also be immediately visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are expected to actively engage with the authors until the issues you have raised for discussion have been sufficiently explored. During this process, be respectful and abide by the Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual quota and assignment responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: By default, TMLR will not assign you more than six reviews per year; the default quota is 6 papers per year but can be changed via the OpenReview console.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may mark yourself temporarily unavailable for periods such as illness, vacation or work leave. You are expected to perform all review assignments that fall within your expertise and quota. Acceptable exceptions include having an unsubmitted review for another TMLR submission. After assignment, OpenReview will ask you to acknowledge the review assignment a couple days later so the AE has confirmation you are aware and will submit on time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review deadlines and final recommendation timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be submitted within 2 weeks of their assignment by the AE for submissions up to 12 pages (main content, before references), and 4 weeks for submissions over 12 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two weeks after all reviewers have submitted their review and the discussion with the authors has started (and no later than 1 month), each reviewer will then be allowed to submit a final decision recommendation to the AE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are responsible for ensuring affiliation and education/career history information is up to date in their OpenReview profile so conflicts can be enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TMLR considers in conflict any individual or institution with which you have shared a collaboration within the past three years. After assignment, if you suspect or believe you have a conflict with any of the authors, consult with the AE for next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of LLMs and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are expected to have read the paper themselves, formed their own opinion, and take responsibility for the writing of their reviews. Reviewers can use LLMs and other tools to assist in these tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable to use LLMs to help find the definition of notation, refine grammar or polish language, or check whether a review is aligned with TMLR's criteria. However, reviewers should form their own internal understanding of the paper and write a review that reflects and expresses their own opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission acceptance standard (reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be written in light of TMLR's Acceptance Criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the separate 'Acceptance Criteria' page for the detailed standard that reviews should use when judging submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review format — summary of contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: A review should include a brief description, in the reviewer's words, of the contributions of the submission, including a list of any key strengths and/or weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary should be concise and reflect the reviewer's understanding of the paper's claimed contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: TMLR decision criterion: Are claims supported?
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims made in the submission supported by accurate, convincing and clear evidence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a Yes/No answer to this criterion along with an explanation that justifies your judgment (pointing to experiments, proofs, analyses, or missing evidence as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: TMLR decision criterion: Audience interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Would at least some individuals in TMLR's audience be interested in knowing the findings of this paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a Yes/No answer to this criterion along with an explanation describing the paper's likely interest or relevance to the TMLR readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requested changes (revision guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of proposed adjustments to the submission, specifying for each whether they are critical to securing your recommendation for acceptance or would simply strengthen the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about which items are blockers for acceptance vs. which are suggestions for improvement. This helps during discussion and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader impact concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief description of any concerns on the ethical implications of the work that would require adding a Broader Impact Statement (if one is not present) or that are not sufficiently addressed in the Broader Impact Statement section (if one is present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether the paper needs an explicit Broader Impact Statement or revisions to the existing statement, and be specific about the ethical risks or societal implications you identify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement in post-review discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately after submitting your review, the crucial period of discussion with the authors starts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You should engage with the authors by responding to their requests for clarifications, acknowledging the changes they make to their submission, and signal to them as soon as you are willing to recommend acceptance. Active engagement is expected until issues have been sufficiently explored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official decision recommendation options
rubrics_metrics.description: After the post-review discussion window, reviewers will be asked for a decision recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation choices are: accept, leaning accept, leaning reject or reject. The recommendation should reflect your judgment after initial assessment and the discussion with the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification recommendations and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to submit recommendations for certifications (Outstanding, Featured, Expert Reviewer, Reproducibility, Survey) which highlight notable accepted submissions and enable editorial judgement on significance/impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification selection is the responsibility of the AE, but reviewers should nominate papers for certifications and provide supporting rationale. Certifications can affect later recognition (e.g., journal-to-conference track eligibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding Certification criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded to papers which are deemed to be exceptionally high quality and broadly significant for the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification may be given well after initial publication and is equivalent to a best paper award at a top-tier conference; reviewers can recommend but final award is by the editorial board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Featured Certification criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: May be awarded to papers that are very high quality, presenting significant contributions which are novel, clearly explained, and well supported with evidence, theory, or analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such papers, if submitted to a top-tier conference, would likely be presented as an oral/spotlight. Reviewers can recommend Featured Certification with justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert Reviewer Certification criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded to papers that are authored by highly-rated TMLR reviewers, to recognize their contributions and expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification is based on author identity being a highly-rated reviewer; reviewers may recommend but selection requires approval by at least one editor-in-chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility Certification criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded to papers whose primary purpose is reproduction of other published work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond simple verification, the paper must contribute significant added value through additional baselines, analysis, ablations, or insights. Reviewers recommending this certification should justify the added value provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey Certification criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that not only meet the criteria for acceptance but also provide an exceptionally thorough or insightful survey of the topic or approach may be awarded this certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should indicate why the survey is exceptional (coverage, synthesis, perspective) when recommending this certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal-to-Conference (J2C) recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked whether they recommend the work to the NeurIPS/ICLR/ICML Journal-to-Conference Track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewers' recommendation, along with that of the Action Editor, will determine whether the TMLR submission will receive a J2C Certification. See the track’s website for details and eligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review evaluation by Action Editor
rubrics_metrics.description: The Action Editor will monitor the discussion and consult the reviewers' feedback and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making a decision, the AE will also evaluate and rate your review. Provide clear, constructive, and well-justified reviews because they will be assessed by the AE.
